requirement: Compute validation loss for a PyTorch model with dropout and batch norm in eval mode and autograd disabled, leaving the model in whatever mode it was in before.
skeleton: An evaluate function saving the training flag, switching to eval, looping under no_grad inside try, restoring the flag in finally, rejecting zero batches, and returning the mean loss.
caption: A PyTorch-style validation loop, written in the standard library against a duck-typed model with a training flag, eval and train methods, and an injected no_grad context manager factory, with no third-party imports. evaluate(model, batches, loss_fn, no_grad) remembers model.training, calls model.eval(), and inside a try block enters no_grad() and sums float(loss_fn(model(inputs), targets)) over the batches while counting them. A finally clause calls model.train with the remembered flag, so a model that was already in eval mode stays there and the mode is restored even when the forward pass raises. With no batches it raises ValueError saying no batches to evaluate; otherwise it returns the mean loss. The fixture asserts the mean, that forward passes run in eval mode with gradients disabled, that train and eval modes are restored, restoration after an exception, and the empty case.

constraints: Forward passes run after model.eval() inside no_grad()
The original training flag is restored with model.train(flag)
The mode is restored in a finally block even on error

rationale.teaches: Save model.training, call eval, run the loop inside no_grad within try, and restore with train(was_training) in finally.
rationale.why: Forgetting eval keeps dropout active and skews metrics, restoring with train() flips an eval-only model into training, and building graphs during validation wastes memory.

ops.docstring: Evaluate a torch-style model in eval mode under no_grad, then restore it.

ops.source:
def evaluate(
    model: Any,
    batches: Iterable[tuple[Any, Any]],
    loss_fn: Callable[[Any, Any], Any],
    no_grad: Callable[[], AbstractContextManager[Any]],
) -> float:
    """Return the mean batch loss without tracking gradients."""
    was_training = model.training
    model.eval()
    total = 0.0
    count = 0
    try:
        with no_grad():
            for inputs, targets in batches:
                total += float(loss_fn(model(inputs), targets))
                count += 1
    finally:
        model.train(was_training)
    if count == 0:
        raise ValueError("no batches to evaluate")
    return total / count

candidates.why_wrong: The forward pass runs in training mode with dropout still active.
A model that was in eval mode is left in training mode afterwards.
An exception in the forward pass leaves the model stuck in eval mode.
The loop runs outside no_grad, so autograd graphs are built for validation.
Empty batches crash with ZeroDivisionError instead of ValueError.
